topicGaps: General pediatric breadth remains the largest video gap: no comparable current recorded coverage was verified for ordinary ambulatory pediatrics, newborn/infant care, ED/inpatient/PICU/NICU and developmental-behavioral/adolescent medicine.
Hands-on physical examination, dysmorphology assessment, procedural skill, supervised case exposure and clinical judgment cannot be acquired or assessed through these recordings or scripts.

Time-critical metabolic decompensation, biochemical test interpretation, disorder-specific confirmation and state newborn-screen follow-up still need source-checked, local-protocol-specific supervised instruction; the packet’s original CDC content distinguishes population screening from diagnosis.

The added GenQA recordings improve exposure to variant-analysis tools, assay sensitivity/CNV interpretation and databases, but are laboratory-centred and do not replace clinical genetics supervision or current patient-specific laboratory interpretation.

Phenotype-first pediatric evaluation, assay selection across CMA/ES/GS/repeat/methylation mechanisms, VUS communication, consent/secondary findings, and developmental assessment remain insufficiently covered by the public recordings and are addressed in authored scripts only as education.

Most pre-existing NHGRI recordings are approximately 12–14 years old. Therapeutic indications, screening panels, eligibility, board rules and any time-sensitive claims must be rechecked against current authoritative sources before use.
medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A child has unexplained developmental delay and multiple congenital anomalies. Which statement best reflects the 2021 ACMG evidence-based guideline for pediatric patients with CA/DD/ID?

options.text: ES/GS should only be considered after every available single-gene test is negative.
ES/GS should be considered as a first- or second-tier test, guided by clinical judgment and shared decision-making.
A positive ES/GS result removes the need for phenotype review.
ES/GS is contraindicated before school age.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACMG strongly recommends ES/GS as a first- or second-tier test for specified pediatric congenital anomaly or DD/ID presentations. The choice is guided by clinical judgment, context and family discussion; limitations and complementary testing still matter.

practiceQuestions.stem: A sequence variant is reported as a variant of uncertain significance (VUS). Which is the most defensible educational interpretation?

options.text: Treat it as pathogenic if phenotype overlap is plausible.
Use it alone to direct irreversible management.
Do not use the VUS alone for clinical decision-making; assess evidence and consider appropriate follow-up/reanalysis.
It is equivalent to likely benign.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACMG/AMP five-tier terminology separates uncertain significance from pathogenic and benign categories; a VUS is not a definitive diagnosis. Interpretation belongs with qualified clinical/laboratory expertise and clinical context.

practiceQuestions.stem: A state newborn-screening laboratory flags an infant’s dried blood spot. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The screen alone establishes the diagnosis.
A screen-positive result requires timely follow-up and appropriate confirmatory evaluation; screening and diagnosis are distinct.
The family should wait for symptoms before follow-up.
The same panel and follow-up schedule are identical in every state.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Newborn screening is a population screening system; abnormal results need appropriate communication and follow-up. State programs and conditions differ, so local protocols and responsible clinicians matter.

practiceQuestions.stem: A trio exome report identifies a candidate variant, but the referral note contains only “developmental delay.” Which action best supports interpretation?

options.text: Send the lab only the variant so the phenotype cannot bias analysis.
Improve the structured phenotype and family history provided to the laboratory, then interpret with test limitations and segregation in mind.
Assume any de novo variant is causal.
Ignore examination findings once sequencing is complete.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Phenotype information is important for interpretation. Trio relationships and segregation can aid prioritization but do not prove causality; evidence and technical limitations remain relevant.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which finding is a known limitation of chromosomal microarray?

options.text: It cannot identify any copy-number changes.
It does not reliably detect balanced chromosome rearrangements.
It is a diagnostic test for all repeat expansions.
It directly measures all methylation abnormalities.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CMA detects genome-wide dosage changes but generally does not identify balanced rearrangements; its capabilities depend on platform and do not replace mechanism-directed methods.

practiceQuestions.stem: A family asks whether a free online course and a completed self-study certificate can make a learner eligible for the ABMGG clinical genetics board examination. Which answer is correct?

options.text: Yes; a 36-hour course is equivalent to accredited combined residency.
No; ABMGG eligibility requires the board-defined accredited training pathway and other applicable requirements.
Yes; any MD or DO may sit after the course.
Yes, if a course uses board-style questions.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABMGG identifies accredited clinical genetics and genomics residency/combined training pathways; an independent educational course neither replaces accredited training nor grants board eligibility.

practiceQuestions.stem: An online public database contains conflicting variant assertions submitted by different laboratories. What is the safest educational response?

options.text: Choose the newest assertion and call the diagnosis.
Treat the database as one evidence source; inspect provenance, classification date, phenotype and expert review, and defer clinical interpretation to qualified professionals.
Resolve the conflict by majority vote of submitters.
Ignore variant classification and infer from a disease name.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Public variant databases aggregate assertions with varying evidence and dates. A clinical interpretation requires source assessment and full laboratory/phenotype context.

practiceQuestions.stem: A caregiver receives a nondiagnostic exome report. Which follow-up explanation is most appropriate?

options.text: A negative report proves the condition is not genetic.
A nondiagnostic result can reflect assay limitations, current knowledge or the phenotype; additional targeted testing or reanalysis may be appropriate in context.
Repeat the same test monthly.
Any VUS should be presented as the likely diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ES/GS has limitations and a nondiagnostic result does not rule out genetic disease. Additional testing or later reanalysis may be considered by the treating clinical genetics team.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement distinguishes Hopkins’s combined residency from an adjacent research postdoctoral offering?

options.text: They are the same credential with different names.
The combined pediatrics–medical genetics programme is a four-year physician residency; research postdoctoral and laboratory programmes are distinct categories.
The combined residency is a genetic counseling internship.
A research appointment itself permits ABP and ABMGG certification.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Hopkins lists the combined physician residency separately from research postdoctoral and laboratory training offerings. Do not infer board eligibility from directory proximity or generic labels.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which description of the boards for this combined pathway is most accurate?

options.text: One joint exam replaces all component certification.
The training pathway is designed to support eligibility for separate ABP and ABMGG examinations after programme and board requirements are met.
ABMGG has no clinical genetics examination.
The ABP examination can be taken before completing combined training in any case.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABP describes a four-year pediatrics–medical genetics agreement and states the ABP exam is not available until all four years are completed; ABMGG certification remains separate and subject to its own rules.

assignment.title: Integrated developmental-behavioral formulation portfolio (self-study only)
tasks: Produce a fictional, clearly labeled developmental history and strength-based problem representation; include age/context, domains, trajectory, function, informants and family priorities.
Choose screening/assessment options and state purpose, psychometric/linguistic limits and follow-up/referral.
Create a prioritized differential and justified, proportionate medical/genetic/behavioral evaluation; identify urgent red flags and what is not indicated routinely.
Draft a family-facing feedback/referral plan covering early intervention, school supports and one relevant transition/equity consideration.
Complete a one-page evidence appraisal or QI storyboard with outcome/process measure, balancing measure, privacy, ethics and limitations.

rubric.standard: Domains, trajectory and context represented; alternatives and uncertainty explicit.
Purpose and limits of instruments clear; distinction screening/diagnosis.
No unjustified broad tests or treatment claims; red flags and contemporary source checks.
Strengths-based, culturally and linguistically responsive, practical pathway.
Accurate citations, coherent communication, privacy/ethics and limitations.

assignment.passRule: Formative score only; suggested mastery threshold 80% with revision on safety/domain omissions. Not predictive of ABP performance.

formative: 12 unit retrieval quizzes (5-10 items each, draft for self-study)
Case formulation and feedback reflection after units 2, 4, 7, and 10
Evidence appraisal and small QI storyboard
assessment.summative: 10 original, cited practice questions and integrated portfolio; no proprietary questions. Not validated as a board simulation or passing predictor.
assessment.rubricScale: 0–4: 0 absent/unsafe; 1 major omission; 2 partial with important gaps; 3 accurate and reasoned; 4 accurate, nuanced, sourced and family-centered.

studyHours.basis: Transparent independent-study plan only, not training hours: approx 36h verified-plus-target lecture viewing, 30h guided reading, 30h case/assignment work, 12h retrieval/practice, 12h portfolio/QI and reflection. The actual ready lecture subset is presently much shorter than 36h; remaining planned-film time is not available media. Clinical supervision and direct patient care hours are zero.

unitMap.text: Developmental science, surveillance, and screening
Developmental history, examination, and assessment literacy
Global developmental delay and intellectual disability
Autism spectrum and social communication
ADHD, executive function, and learning
Language, speech, literacy, and academic achievement
Genetic syndromes and medical/neurodevelopmental complexity
Mental health, behavior, sleep, feeding, and regulation
Neurologic, motor, sensory, and complex disability
Family partnership, equity, social context, and advocacy
Adolescence, sexuality, transition, and safeguarding
Scholarship, teaching, quality improvement, and professional practice

topicGaps: Autism diagnostic assessment, criteria, screening-versus-diagnosis and evidence-based care remain insufficiently covered by verified recordings; current CDC/AAP readings remain essential.
ADHD multi-informant evaluation, differential diagnosis, guideline-based treatment choices and monitoring lack a verified full-length recording.
Speech-language, communication and academic learning disorders have partial autism-seminar coverage but need fuller assessment, bilingual and school-interface teaching.

Syndrome/genetics, global developmental delay/intellectual disability etiologic reasoning and complex care remain only partly covered; the existing ID grand rounds and open readings are not a full course.

Mental health, sleep, feeding and regulation now have several focused autism recordings, but general child mental-health assessment, safety and intervention evidence still need current, broader instruction.
Motor, sensory, neurologic and medical complexity remain insufficiently covered by specialty recordings; the new epilepsy session is only a focused partial contribution.
Family-school advocacy, IDEA/504 and jurisdiction-specific eligibility, accessible sexuality, safeguarding and transition remain only partly covered despite one autism-to-adulthood recording.
Scholarship, QI, teaching and professional practice need additional source-grounded instruction.
Observed eligible recordings total 12.866389 hours; 23.133611 hours remain to the 36-hour floor. Authored scripts are planned content and add zero rendered hours.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

boardNames: American Board of Pediatrics (ABP) — Developmental-Behavioral Pediatrics subspecialty certifying examination
medical.boardStatus: ABP subspecialty certificate/examination exists; separate from general pediatrics certification. ABP page checked 2026-10-07 and identifies its distinct subspecialty certifying exam.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: Educational self-study is not fellowship training or certification eligibility. ABP currently requires three years full-time broad-based training in ACGME- or RCPSC-accredited DBP program, verified training, scholarly activity and passing the exam; general criteria include ABP General Pediatrics certification/maintenance, unrestricted US/Canada license, training verification and further time-limited requirements. Verify current ABP rules directly.

officialProgrammes.institution: Boston Children’s Hospital (Harvard Medical School appointment noted by programme; programme is not Harvard-operated simply by that appointment)
officialProgrammes.name: Developmental-Behavioral Pediatrics Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page calls it a three-year ACGME-accredited clinical, didactic and research fellowship; entry at PL-4 or later; weekly DBP seminar has rotating two-year content outline, neurology/psychiatry courses, longitudinal and multidisciplinary clinical experiences, community ASK work, electives, research/QI. Public description is not an actual full lecture schedule or complete curriculum-hour record.

medical.programmeSourceScope: Official Boston Children’s programme supplied in item packet; Johns Hopkins official fellowship directory checked and DBP not listed. No verified Johns Hopkins variant or separate Harvard-operated programme found. Programme claims reflect its public page, not private didactics. No combined programme verified.
sourceCaveats: Johns Hopkins directory checked 2026-10-07 lists many pediatric fellowship specialties but not DBP; no Hopkins DBP fellowship variant verified. A Johns Hopkins child-development clinical service or generic directory entry is not proof of DBP physician fellowship.
Only Boston Children’s official fellowship is an institutional variant in this packet. Do not infer separate Harvard Medical School-operated programme from its fellows’ concurrent HMS appointments.
No combined DBP fellowship/board pathway verified. The ABP offers a separate DBP subspecialty certifying examination.
Clinical training page, ACGME requirements/milestones, and ABP certification blueprint are distinct sources and not interchangeable.
A public lecture listing or free course is not institutional fellowship credit. Free CHOP OPEN lectures require account/enrollment and have copyright restrictions; excluded from the counted hours.
Several UW curriculum video runtimes are published approximately (e.g. “~52 minutes”) and video metadata extraction failed; they are cataloged as uncounted candidates, not counted as observed media.

AAP player stateless metadata showed duration unavailable; for two AAP recordings, counted only the publisher’s explicit rounded 1-hour and 25-minute labels. Their exact timecodes were not independently probed.
No human clinical review performed. Clinical source check as of 2026-10-07; board rules, practice guidelines, licensing, referrals, services and legal rules may change.

No patient-level advice, clinical assessment, supervised experience, diagnosis, case-volume claim, procedure competence, licensure, ABP eligibility, accreditation, affiliation, or guaranteed exam result.

Speech-language, communication and academic learning disorders have partial autism-seminar coverage but need fuller assessment, bilingual and school-interface teaching.

Syndrome/genetics, global developmental delay/intellectual disability etiologic reasoning and complex care remain only partly covered; the existing ID grand rounds and open readings are not a full course.

Mental health, sleep, feeding and regulation now have several focused autism recordings, but general child mental-health assessment, safety and intervention evidence still need current, broader instruction.
Motor, sensory, neurologic and medical complexity remain insufficiently covered by specialty recordings; the new epilepsy session is only a focused partial contribution.
Family-school advocacy, IDEA/504 and jurisdiction-specific eligibility, accessible sexuality, safeguarding and transition remain only partly covered despite one autism-to-adulthood recording.

medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: At a well visit, a caregiver reports persistent communication concern despite a milestone checklist that appears reassuring. Which next step best reflects developmental surveillance practice?

options.text: Reassure because checklist completion excludes developmental disorder.
Explore the concern and trajectory, perform or arrange validated screening/assessment as indicated, and plan follow-up/referral.
Diagnose autism from the caregiver’s report.
Wait until school entry before acting.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Monitoring materials do not replace validated screening; persistent concern warrants responsive evaluation and follow-up rather than dismissal or premature diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.stem: A 30-month-old has language delay and a developmental screen above its referral threshold. What is the most accurate interpretation?

options.text: The screen establishes intellectual disability.
The screen indicates elevated concern and need for further evaluation; it does not determine etiology or establish diagnosis.
No further steps are needed if motor skills are typical.
A broad metabolic panel is required in every child.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Screening identifies risk, not a diagnosis. Evaluation integrates history, function, examination and appropriately selected testing.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best describes the diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder?

options.text: A blood test confirms ASD.
Diagnosis is based on developmental/behavioral evidence, with consideration of differential and co-occurring conditions.
A positive screening score is diagnostic.
A child must have intellectual disability.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC notes no medical test such as a blood test diagnoses ASD; clinicians consider development and behavior. Screening alone is not diagnostic.

practiceQuestions.stem: A child with ASD has no seizure history, atypical regression, or neurologic red flags. Which approach to EEG is most consistent with the AAP clinical report?

options.text: Order routine baseline EEG for every autistic child.
EEG is not routinely indicated absent clinical concern; investigate if seizure concern, atypical regression or other neurologic signs arise.
EEG confirms autism.
Never obtain EEG in a child with ASD.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The report does not recommend routine baseline EEG without clinical indications, but supports evaluation when relevant neurologic concerns exist.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional 8-year-old meets a teacher checklist threshold for ADHD but has normal classroom behavior in another setting and severe sleep disruption. What is the best reasoning step?

options.text: Diagnose ADHD solely from one checklist.
Integrate multi-informant, multi-setting evidence and assess sleep and other differential contributors before formulating diagnosis and plan.
Dismiss the teacher report.
Start medication without evaluation.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ADHD assessment depends on impairment and evidence across contexts; sleep, learning, language, mental health and other factors may mimic or co-occur. Check current guideline before clinical use.

practiceQuestions.stem: A young child with suspected developmental delay has lost previously acquired words and now has episodes concerning for seizures. What is the best general response?

options.text: Assume autism regression and defer evaluation.
Treat regression and possible seizure symptoms as red flags requiring prompt focused medical/neurologic assessment.
Order the same full metabolic panel for all children.
Wait for a school eligibility decision.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Regression and possible seizures require careful prompt assessment. Evaluation should be guided by history/exam and specialist judgment, not an indiscriminate fixed battery.

practiceQuestions.stem: A caregiver asks whether they may contact early intervention before a medical diagnosis is complete. Which response is most accurate?

options.text: They must wait for a specialist diagnosis.
They may contact the local public early-childhood system to ask about evaluation; age and state processes determine the pathway.
Only schools can evaluate children under three.
A referral guarantees program eligibility.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC advises families can request public early-intervention evaluation without waiting for physician referral or diagnosis; eligibility and implementation vary.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which evidence most directly supports an intellectual disability formulation rather than isolated low achievement?

options.text: A single low classroom grade.
Integrated evidence of limitations in intellectual functioning and adaptive functioning with developmental onset, interpreted in context.
One screening score without functional history.
A genetic variant of uncertain significance alone.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ID formulation requires integrated cognitive and adaptive-function evidence, developmental context and differential; no isolated grade or variant suffices.

practiceQuestions.stem: During feedback, the clinician finds caregiver language preference differs from the clinic’s default language. Which action best supports equitable developmental care?

options.text: Use a child sibling as interpreter to save time.
Ask preferred language and arrange qualified language access; communicate strengths, uncertainty and next steps in understandable terms.
Assume language difference explains delay.
Exclude caregiver observations.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Family partnership requires accessible communication and interpretation that preserves the caregiver’s contribution; multilingualism alone is not disorder.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about ABP developmental-behavioral pediatrics certification is correct as checked 2026-10-07?

options.text: Completion of an independent online curriculum alone meets certification eligibility.
ABP identifies a subspecialty certifying examination and requires accredited fellowship training, training verification/scholarly activity and other general eligibility criteria.
No separate examination exists.
A certificate is guaranteed after three years in any educational programme.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABP describes a distinct subspecialty examination and required three-year full-time accredited fellowship, verification and scholarly activity; general criteria include general pediatrics certification, licensure and other conditions.

title: General Academic Pediatrics Fellowship

prerequisites.level: Advanced post-residency/professional self-study for pediatric clinicians, fellows, faculty and doctoral researchers. It is not an entry-level clinical curriculum or fellowship substitute.

Basic epidemiology and statistics helpful but introduced from first principles.
Research and education units are also useful to doctorally trained non-physician learners; clinical units are for education only, not scope expansion.
prerequisites.boundaries: No individual patient diagnosis/treatment, supervised clinical practice, licensure, board eligibility, clinical privileges, procedure competence or institutional credential is conferred.

topicGaps: Specialty-specific pediatric/academic-generalist footage totals 2.4642 h across three duration-verified recordings: the pre-existing child-poverty/disparities lecture (47:12), a PAS 2024 complex-care research recording (39:55), and the public HEAL Pediatric Health Equity webinar (1:00:44). This remains short of the 36-hour specialty-specific target by 33.5358 h. The 35.7714 h of newly counted NIH IPPCR media are cross-specialty clinical-research foundations and do not close the specialty-specific gap.

No verified public recording set was found here for broad pediatric preventive-care and clinical board domains (well-child care, growth/development, immunization application, screening, acute/chronic pediatric care); static guidelines/readings are not counted as video hours.

No qualifying freely viewable, duration-verified series was established here for academic-pediatrics medical education, detailed qualitative analysis/mixed-method integration, QI implementation in pediatric practice, advocacy/policy, mentorship/leadership, or complex-care coordination. APA’s webinar library is member-only or $50/webinar, so it is not a free source for this task.

The public NIH IPPCR research lectures address methods, ethics, safety, participant selection, data, protocol, and implementation, but do not replace pediatric subspecialty/clinical instruction, an institutional fellowship, supervised patient care, or local IRB determinations.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

medical.trackType: Non-ACGME clinical physician fellowship (Boston Children’s listing); JHU institutional General Pediatrics Fellowship is research-focused and includes physician and non-physician doctorally trained trainees; APA fellowship accreditation is not ACGME/board certification
boardNames: American Board of Pediatrics (ABP) — General Pediatrics certification examination only; no separate Academic General Pediatrics board examination
medical.boardStatus: Academic General Pediatrics has no separate board certification. APA lists an academic general pediatrics fellowship accreditation category; that is distinct from ACGME program accreditation and ABP certification. General pediatrics board certification is a separate exam with separate eligibility requirements.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This course confers no eligibility. Refer to ABP General Pediatrics admission requirements and the candidate’s own accredited residency/board status; fellowship participation or course completion does not establish eligibility. No passing outcome is promised.

officialProgrammes.institution: Boston Children’s Hospital / Harvard Medical School teaching hospital
officialProgrammes.name: General Academic Pediatrics Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page describes three-year academic leadership fellowship. Public curriculum states first year primarily clinical with six clinical/precepting sessions weekly, later reduced clinical responsibilities and research work, teaching, advocacy, seminars and coursework. Directory marks APA-accredited; packet identifies BCH GME directory as non-ACGME. No institutional lecture recordings/complete syllabus are supplied here.

officialProgrammes.institution: Johns Hopkins University / Johns Hopkins Children’s Center
officialProgrammes.name: General Pediatrics Fellowship (APA directory label: Johns Hopkins University Primary Care Research Fellowship Program)
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page calls it General Pediatrics Fellowship, with primary-care/population-health and health-disparities research. At least 80% time research training; individualized coursework/seminars, physician fellows precept and candidates may be physicians or other doctorally trained people. APA directory names the Primary Care Research Fellowship Program and marks it accredited. Preserve the institutional naming difference. This is not represented as an identical clinical fellowship to BCH.

medical.programmeSourceScope: The item packet supplied Boston Children’s Hospital as official program. Research identifies Johns Hopkins as a distinct exact institutional variant in the APA directory: JHU official page uses General Pediatrics Fellowship; APA directory uses Johns Hopkins University Primary Care Research Fellowship Program. Both are academic general pediatrics/primary-care research fellowship variants, with notable JHU non-physician eligibility and >80% research training. Generic directory category does not itself mean physician-only or ACGME clinical accreditation. Research-only/non-physician participation at JHU is noted, not conflated with physician clinical training. No additional institutional variant is asserted.
sourceCaveats: The CDC page currently reports that, following the stated March 16, 2026 court order, the July 2, 2025 schedule is the current CDC schedule; vaccine recommendations are legally and clinically date-sensitive. Re-check CDC, AAP and relevant local guidance before clinical use.
Institutional websites and APA directory can change; dates above reflect public pages accessed 2026-10-07.
ABP content outline PDF applies effective October 15, 2024, with minor revisions in December 2024; ABP webpage last updated Nov. 25, 2025.
ABP outline is a clinical pediatrics certification blueprint, not a complete academic-fellowship competency framework. APA competencies are used for research, education, leadership and advocacy.

YouTube metadata extraction for several unrelated candidates failed or topic fit was uncertain; those videos were excluded. Count only the 47:12 publicly viewable poverty/disparities video whose exact player duration appeared on the fetched page.
No clinical expert review was performed. Case links are for source-site viewing only; no clinical images or patient records are copied.

topicGaps: Specialty-specific pediatric/academic-generalist footage totals 2.4642 h across three duration-verified recordings: the pre-existing child-poverty/disparities lecture (47:12), a PAS 2024 complex-care research recording (39:55), and the public HEAL Pediatric Health Equity webinar (1:00:44). This remains short of the 36-hour specialty-specific target by 33.5358 h. The 35.7714 h of newly counted NIH IPPCR media are cross-specialty clinical-research foundations and do not close the specialty-specific gap.

No verified public recording set was found here for broad pediatric preventive-care and clinical board domains (well-child care, growth/development, immunization application, screening, acute/chronic pediatric care); static guidelines/readings are not counted as video hours.

No qualifying freely viewable, duration-verified series was established here for academic-pediatrics medical education, detailed qualitative analysis/mixed-method integration, QI implementation in pediatric practice, advocacy/policy, mentorship/leadership, or complex-care coordination. APA’s webinar library is member-only or $50/webinar, so it is not a free source for this task.

The public NIH IPPCR research lectures address methods, ethics, safety, participant selection, data, protocol, and implementation, but do not replace pediatric subspecialty/clinical instruction, an institutional fellowship, supervised patient care, or local IRB determinations.
medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A clinic wants to know whether an outreach reminder improves well-child visit completion. Which design best supports estimating the intervention’s effect while accounting for secular changes?

options.text: Compare rates before and after in a single clinic only
Randomize eligible clinic panels to reminder versus usual outreach if feasible, prespecifying outcomes
Interview only families who attended
Compare clinic rate with a national rate from a different year

practiceQuestions.rationale: A prespecified concurrent comparison, ideally randomized where appropriate and ethical, better separates intervention effects from secular trends. A simple pre/post comparison is vulnerable to confounding and time trends.

practiceQuestions.stem: A published pediatric intervention reports a relative risk reduction but gives no baseline risk. What is the most defensible interpretation?

options.text: The absolute benefit can be calculated exactly
Clinical importance cannot be judged from relative reduction alone without baseline risk and uncertainty
The intervention has no benefit
The result proves benefit for every clinic

practiceQuestions.rationale: Relative effects do not determine absolute risk difference or number needed to treat without baseline risk; uncertainty and external validity also matter.

practiceQuestions.stem: A team is screening families for social needs. Which approach best aligns an equity-focused academic generalist practice?

options.text: Treat a positive screen as proof of an individual family’s cause of illness
Ask permission, explain purpose and privacy, offer feasible supports, and evaluate whether workflows improve access without stigma
Require disclosure before care
Use neighborhood race as a substitute for individual needs

practiceQuestions.rationale: Screening should be respectful and connected to action; avoid causal assumptions and stigmatizing labels. Equity evaluation should assess access and unintended effects.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fellow plans to interview caregivers about barriers to clinic access. Which practice strengthens qualitative rigor?

options.text: Use leading questions to confirm the team’s favored explanation
Describe sampling rationale, reflexivity, analytic process and how divergent accounts were handled
Claim generalizability from a small purposive sample without qualification
Stop coding once the first expected theme appears

practiceQuestions.rationale: Transparent sampling, reflexivity and analytic documentation support credibility; divergent findings and limits should be reported rather than suppressed.

practiceQuestions.stem: An education group wants to know whether a new seminar improves residents’ counseling skills. What is the best initial evaluation plan?

options.text: Measure satisfaction only and claim competence
Align a behavioral outcome with the objective, use a structured observation/rubric, and consider baseline and follow-up evidence
Count seminar attendance as skill acquisition
Use an unrelated knowledge test

practiceQuestions.rationale: Assessment should align with the target competency; direct structured observation is more relevant than satisfaction or attendance alone.

practiceQuestions.stem: A local QI team sees improvement after a workflow change and wants to assert that the change caused the improvement. What is the best response?

options.text: Report association and time pattern, examine context and balancing measures, and avoid causal certainty without a design supporting it
Claim causation because improvement followed the change
Ignore balancing measures
Generalize to all hospitals

practiceQuestions.rationale: Local QI data can guide learning but temporal association alone does not establish causality. Context, measurement quality, and unintended effects matter.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fellow cannot tell whether a proposed clinic workflow project is QI, human-subjects research, or both. What should they do?

options.text: Self-declare it exempt and begin interviews
Consult their institutional IRB/QI determination pathway before collecting research data
Ask participants to sign a generic form instead
Avoid any documentation

practiceQuestions.rationale: The distinction and review requirements are context- and institution-dependent. Trainees should not self-issue IRB determinations.

practiceQuestions.stem: A pediatrician asks whether completion of an academic general pediatrics fellowship provides a separate specialty board certificate. Which answer is accurate?

options.text: Yes, ABP offers an Academic General Pediatrics subspecialty certificate
No separate Academic Generalist certification is described; ABP general pediatrics certification is distinct and has its own eligibility
APA fellowship accreditation is an ABMS board exam
Completion automatically grants general pediatric board eligibility

practiceQuestions.rationale: APA explicitly says no separate certification exists for academic generalists beyond the general pediatrics examination; fellowship accreditation is not board certification or eligibility.
